title: Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
summary: Google introduced Agent2Agent (A2A), an open protocol for communication between AI agents built by different vendors and on different frameworks, with the draft specification published on GitHub. Google says the launch had backing from more than 50 technology partners plus services firms such as Accenture, Deloitte and KPMG. The post positions A2A as complementary to Anthropic's MCP: MCP supplies tools and context to an agent, while A2A handles agent-to-agent communication.
relevance: This is the origin event for the dominant open standard for cross-vendor task delegation between agents.
search_query: Google announces Agent2Agent protocol A2A April 2025
notes: Fetched page does not name a license; secondary sources state Apache 2.0.

title: Empowering multi-agent apps with the open Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol
summary: Microsoft announced that A2A support was coming to Azure AI Foundry and Copilot Studio, with a public preview promised soon but no date given. Microsoft says it joined the A2A working group on GitHub, that agents built with Semantic Kernel or LangChain can interoperate over A2A, and that calls would be protected with Microsoft Entra, mutual TLS, content safety and audit logs. A Semantic Kernel Python sample showed two local agents collaborating.
relevance: A second hyperscaler adopting a Google-originated protocol was an early signal that A2A could serve as a cross-vendor delegation layer.

title: ServiceNow Launches AI Control Tower and AI Agent Fabric at Knowledge 2025
summary: At its Knowledge 2025 conference, ServiceNow launched AI Agent Fabric, which it describes as a communication backbone that uses MCP and A2A for agent-to-agent, agent-to-tool and system-to-system communication across ServiceNow and third-party agents. It also launched AI Control Tower for governing agents. ServiceNow names Accenture, Adobe, Box, Cisco, Google Cloud, IBM, Jit, Microsoft, Moonhub, RADCOM, UKG and Zoom as offering the first Agent Fabric integrations.
relevance: An enterprise workflow vendor paired an A2A/MCP interop fabric with a central governance plane, a pattern relevant to accountable cross-vendor task movement.

notes: Wire-service reprint of ServiceNow press material (ServiceNow's own press page and Business Wire returned HTTP 403). The underlying ServiceNow release is dated 2025-05-06.

title: Introducing ANS: DNS-Inspired Secure Discovery for AI Agents
summary: InfoQ reported on the Agent Name Service (ANS), proposed under the OWASP GenAI Security Project, a protocol-agnostic registry that uses PKI to verify agent identity before returning an agent's endpoint. ANS names encode protocol, agent ID, capability, provider, version and extension (for example an a2a:// name), and protocol adapters cover A2A, MCP and ACP. The article reports a GitHub prototype and planned work on scalability, zero-knowledge proofs and formal verification, and quotes a reviewer who says broad governance and participation are prerequisites for adoption.
relevance: Verifiable cross-protocol discovery is a precondition for safely handing a task to an agent outside one's own organization.
search_query: OWASP Agent Name Service ANS AI agent discovery DNS news

title: Linux Foundation Launches the Agent2Agent Protocol Project to Enable Secure, Intelligent Communication Between AI Agents
summary: At Open Source Summit North America in Denver, the Linux Foundation announced that it would host the Agent2Agent project, seeded by Google's transfer of the A2A specification, SDKs and tooling, with the repository moving to github.com/a2aproject/A2A. The release cites support from more than 100 technology companies and includes statements from AWS, Cisco (Outshift), Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow. Executive Director Jim Zemlin framed the move as securing vendor-neutral governance.
relevance: Moving A2A to neutral governance reduced single-vendor risk for a protocol meant to carry tasks across organizational boundaries.
search_query: Linux Foundation launches Agent2Agent protocol project

title: Linux Foundation Welcomes the AGNTCY Project to Standardize Open Multi-Agent System Infrastructure and Break Down AI Agent Silos
summary: Cisco contributed AGNTCY, the 'Internet of Agents' infrastructure project it open-sourced in March 2025 with LangChain and Galileo, to the Linux Foundation. Cisco, Dell Technologies, Google Cloud, Oracle and Red Hat joined as formative members, and the release cites more than 65 supporting companies. Components cover agent discovery via the Open Agent Schema Framework (OASF), cryptographic agent identity, the SLIM messaging layer and multi-agent observability, and the project says it interoperates with A2A and MCP.
relevance: AGNTCY targets the discovery, identity, messaging and observability layers around A2A, which are needed for accountable agent-to-agent hand-offs.
search_query: AGNTCY Linux Foundation Cisco Internet of Agents announcement
notes: Secondary coverage cites more than 75 supporters; the LF release says more than 65.

title: Announcing a complete developer toolkit for scaling A2A agents on Google Cloud
summary: Google announced A2A v0.3, adding gRPC support, the ability to sign security cards (agent cards), and extended client support in the Python SDK; it says the ecosystem had grown past 150 organizations. Alongside it, Google added native A2A support in the Agent Development Kit, deployment paths on Agent Engine (announced as coming soon), Cloud Run and GKE, A2A evaluation in Vertex GenAI Evaluation Service, and listing of A2A agents in its AI Agent Marketplace. Partner examples include ServiceNow and Twilio, and community tools such as A2A Inspector and a Technology Compatibility Kit are mentioned.
relevance: Signed agent cards and transport choice (gRPC) address identity and deployment portability for agents that delegate across hosts.

notes: URL slug and HTML title read 'Agent2Agent protocol (A2A) is getting an upgrade'; page heading is as given. Some secondary coverage dates it 2025-07-31; the fetched page shows 2025-08-01.

title: ACP Joins Forces with A2A
summary: IBM Research's Agent Communication Protocol (ACP), launched in March 2025 to power the BeeAI platform, is merging into A2A under the Linux Foundation, and the ACP team is ending active development. Kate Blair joins the A2A Technical Steering Committee for IBM, alongside Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cisco, Salesforce, ServiceNow and SAP. BeeAI agents can become A2A-compliant through an A2AServer adapter and consume external A2A agents through an A2AAgent client, and a migration guide is provided.
relevance: The merger consolidated two competing agent-to-agent protocols and created an explicit protocol-migration path for existing agents.
search_query: IBM Agent Communication Protocol merges with A2A announcement
notes: Page shows a last-updated date of 2025-09-04.

title: Powering AI commerce with the new Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
summary: Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), designed as an extension of A2A and usable with MCP, for agent-initiated payments across cards, stablecoins and real-time bank transfers. AP2 relies on cryptographically signed 'mandates' (an Intent Mandate and a Cart Mandate) that serve as verifiable proof of user authorization and form an audit trail. Google says more than 60 organizations collaborated, including American Express, Mastercard, PayPal, Coinbase, Salesforce and ServiceNow, and it also launched an A2A x402 extension for crypto payments with Coinbase, the Ethereum Foundation and MetaMask.
relevance: AP2's signed mandates are a concrete mechanism for carrying user authority and accountability along with a delegated task.
search_query: Google Agent Payments Protocol AP2 announcement A2A extension

title: Building Trust at Internet Scale: GoDaddy's Agent Name Service Registry for the Agentic AI Marketplace
summary: GoDaddy described an Agent Name Service registry with a registration authority, building on the IETF and OWASP ANS work, so that agents can discover and verify each other. Its trust chain combines customer verification, ACME DNS-01 domain validation, hybrid public/private certificates, DNSSEC-secured records (TXT records pointing to an Agent Card, plus TLSA/DANE pinning) and Merkle-tree transparency logging. GoDaddy said a developer preview would follow in the coming weeks.
relevance: It is an early commercial attempt to anchor agent identity and agent-card discovery in existing DNS/PKI infrastructure.
search_query: GoDaddy Agent Name Service ANS launch AI agents registry
notes: No author is listed; the date comes from the page metadata timestamp.

title: When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems
summary: Unit 42 described 'agent session smuggling', in which a malicious remote agent exploits the stateful, multi-turn nature of an A2A session to inject covert instructions into a victim client agent. Proof-of-concept attacks built with Google's ADK extracted the client's system instructions, tool schemas and chat history, and triggered an unauthorized stock purchase. The authors say this is not a flaw in A2A itself but a consequence of implicit inter-agent trust, and they report no attacks seen in the wild. Proposed mitigations include out-of-band human approval, context grounding, signed agent cards and exposing agent activity to users.
relevance: It shows that delegating to a peer agent opens a new trust boundary and needs identity, provenance and audit controls.
notes: The 'incident' label refers to a demonstrated attack technique; no exploitation was observed in the wild.

title: Introducing agent-to-agent protocol support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
summary: AWS added A2A support to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, which hosts an A2A server (JSON-RPC 2.0 on port 9000) and serves agent cards at /.well-known/agent-card.json. Inbound requests can be authenticated with OAuth 2.0 or IAM SigV4, and outbound access uses IAM execution roles and AgentCore Identity, with VPC/PrivateLink connectivity and session-lifetime settings. A sample incident-response system has a Google ADK host agent route work to a Strands monitoring agent and an OpenAI Agents SDK operations agent.
relevance: It demonstrates managed hosting of cross-framework agents that delegate over A2A, with platform-level identity and session lifecycle.
search_query: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime A2A protocol support announcement
notes: InfoQ covered this on 2025-11-28 (infoq.com/news/2025/11/a2a-amazon-bedrock-agentcore/) and linked it to the Unit 42 session-smuggling research; not listed separately.

title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), Anchored by New Project Contributions Including Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose and AGENTS.md
summary: The Linux Foundation formed the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) as a neutral home for agentic AI projects, launched with Anthropic's MCP, Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md. Platinum members are AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI, with gold members including Cisco, IBM, Salesforce, SAP, Okta and Temporal. The release does not mention A2A.
relevance: AAIF became the umbrella under which the agent-to-tool (MCP) and, later, agent-to-agent (A2A) layers were co-governed.

title: A2A Protocol Ships v1.0: Production-Ready Standard for Agent-to-Agent Communication
summary: The A2A community released v1.0, its first stable specification, governed by a technical steering committee of AWS, Cisco, Google, IBM Research, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow. New features include multi-protocol bindings with version negotiation (JSON+HTTP, gRPC, JSON-RPC), multi-tenancy, Signed Agent Cards for cryptographic identity verification, modernized security flows, and polling, streaming or webhook result delivery. The release includes breaking changes to the interaction protocol, but the agent card can advertise both v0.3 and v1.0 so clients can migrate gradually.
relevance: A stable, versioned wire contract with signed identity is the baseline needed for portable, verifiable delegation across vendors.
search_query: A2A v1.0 announcement Google developers blog "A2A 1.0" stable specification
notes: No individual authors named (credited to the A2A Protocol community). Reached via a redirect from a2a-protocol.org/latest/announcing-1.0/.

title: A2A Protocol Surpasses 150 Organizations, Lands in Major Cloud Platforms, and Sees Enterprise Production Use in First Year
summary: For A2A's first anniversary, the Linux Foundation said more than 150 organizations support the protocol, up from more than 50 at launch, and that it is integrated into Google, Microsoft (Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio) and AWS (Bedrock AgentCore Runtime) platforms. It reported production-ready SDKs in five languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, .NET) and more than 22,000 GitHub stars on the core repository. It claimed production deployments in supply chain, financial services, insurance and IT operations, but gave no count.
relevance: It records A2A adoption metrics one year in, a useful baseline for judging whether cross-vendor delegation is actually used.
notes: Production-use claims come from the foundation and are not independently quantified.

title: A2A v1 Is Here: Cross-Platform Agent Communication in Microsoft Agent Framework for .NET
summary: Microsoft updated the .NET A2A client and hosting packages of Microsoft Agent Framework to the A2A v1 SDK, although the SDK and those packages remain in preview. HTTP+JSON is the default binding, with JSON-RPC as a fallback; agent-card discovery goes through A2ACardResolver; and server registration, endpoint mapping and well-known card serving are now separate steps. Moving from v0.3 to v1 requires code changes, and a migration guide is linked; the example shows a procurement agent handing off to a partner team's compliance agent.
relevance: It documents the practical migration cost of a breaking protocol version for agents that delegate across team and platform boundaries.

title: A New Chapter for A2A: Joining the Agentic AI Foundation
summary: The A2A project announced its acceptance as a Growth Stage project of the Agentic AI Foundation, joining MCP, goose and AGENTS.md under Linux Foundation-directed governance. The post presents A2A as the horizontal agent-to-agent layer complementing MCP's vertical agent-to-tool role, and cites more than 150 backing organizations and native support from major cloud providers. The two specifications remain separate.
relevance: Co-locating the agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool standards under one foundation affects how delegation and tool access will be aligned.

title: Meet the A2A CLI: discover, message, and manage agents from your terminal
summary: The A2A project released an official command-line client, a2a, built on the CLI from the A2A Go SDK and compatible with protocol v1.0. It can fetch agent cards, send messages (with streaming), and expose any stdin/stdout program as an A2A server for demos and testing. It supports JSON-RPC, REST and gRPC transports with plugins, offers JSON output for automation, and ships an Agent Skill so coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex can drive it. It is licensed under Apache 2.0.
relevance: A standard CLI makes A2A delegation scriptable and testable from coding agents, which lowers the barrier to cross-harness task hand-off experiments.
